turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m having chest pain even at rest—upper chest pain that feels like a knife stroke, and it gets worse when I breathe in. I also feel very short of breath, even at rest and with exertion.

I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. One question at a time:

**When did the chest pain start (exact time or how many hours ago), and has it been constant or coming and going?**
It started fairly fast—about 6 out of 10 for how quickly it began. I can’t give an exact time right now, but it’s been going on since it started and it feels constant, not really coming and going.
**Does the pain stay in the upper chest only, or does it spread anywhere (to the arm, jaw, back, or between the shoulder blades)?**
It stays in the upper chest only. It doesn’t really spread anywhere—no arm, jaw, or back pain.
**Do you have any fever, cough, or recent cold/flu symptoms (sore throat, runny nose), or have you been sick in the last week?**
No fever, no cough, and no recent cold or flu symptoms. I haven’t been sick in the last week.
**Does taking a deep breath make the pain significantly worse, and does pressing on the chest wall reproduce the pain?**
Yes, taking a deep breath makes it worse. And yes—pressing on the chest wall can reproduce the pain.
**Any history of asthma/COPD, wheezing, or recent exposure to smoke/chemicals?**
No asthma or COPD. I do smoke cigarettes, but I haven’t had any specific chemical exposure that I know of.
**Do you have any leg symptoms—pain/swelling in one leg—or have you had recent long travel, surgery, or being bedridden?**
No leg pain or swelling in one leg. And no recent long travel, surgery, or being bedridden.
**Have you had any recent vomiting or severe retching, or trouble swallowing, or sudden tearing pain after an episode like that?**
No vomiting or retching, no trouble swallowing, and no sudden tearing pain after an episode like that.
**Do you have any history of heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a prior heart attack—and what’s your age?**
I don’t have any known heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or prior heart attack. I’m 50 years old.
**Are you having any palpitations, fainting/near-fainting, or a sense your heart is racing?**
No fainting or near-fainting, and no palpitations. My main problem is the chest pain and shortness of breath.
**Do you have any leg swelling, or have you noticed your breathing is worse when lying flat (needing extra pillows)?**
No leg swelling. And I haven’t noticed it being worse when lying flat—I can’t say it’s changed like that.
**Any recent rash, hives, itching, or swelling of lips/tongue, or did this start right after a new food/medication/insect sting?**
No rash or hives, and no swelling of lips or tongue. It didn’t start right after any new food, medicine, or insect sting.
**Do you have any sore throat/hoarseness, drooling, or trouble swallowing (especially if it’s getting worse quickly)?**
No sore throat, hoarseness, drooling, or trouble swallowing.
**Any recent severe sore throat or feeling like you can’t clear secretions, or pain with swallowing?**
No, none of that. No pain with swallowing and no feeling like I can’t clear secretions.
**Any recent heavy exertion, lifting, or trauma that could strain the chest wall or ribs?**
No heavy exertion, lifting, or trauma recently.
[DDX] Possible NSTEMI / STEMI, Pulmonary embolism, Acute pulmonary edema, Pneumonia, GERD
